- Vovin s tips page Tricks of the trade: Here are some random tips and tricks I have learned since working on this project. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- I chose to place them here to make the guide less bulky. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Cleanliness is vital. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Placing your liquid into a flask or funnel that has not been cleaned well will result in junk winding up in your extraction. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Clean all your containers thoroughly every time before use. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Don t use regular water. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Some people don t bother with distilled water.  this is one of the worst things you can do. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- You will be using quite a bit of water in this experiment which means a lot of junk. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Distilled water is available in every grocery store on the planet. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- I purchased all of my lab equipment off of ebay. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- It is much cheaper than purchasing from a lab supply store and no questions are asked. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- All of the items I got had very slight cosmetic defects but they did not cause any issues in the functioning of the equipment. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Cling wrap is a excellent tool in covering your flasks and other containers. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- It prevents evaporation and also reduces the chance of spilling the material. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Plus dust and particles can get into your extraction if you don t have something as a lid. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- I use the cling wrap because it can easily be punctured to allow venting while sealing the container as well. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Put a rubber band around the neck to keep it on as well. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- If you are using a 500ml separatory funnel and 500 ml flasks they do have a little more room in them but not a whole lot. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- You can do this during the reducing stage. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- If you plan on making larger batches then buy bigger glassware. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Cutting corners can cost you. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- This is the first hard lesson you will learn. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Do your best to stick to the guide. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- By trying to cut corners you are adding more variables into a already hard situation. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- This leaves a lot more room for error. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- When in doubt stop and ask. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- DMT World is a great place to ask questions. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- It is much easier to put a hold on your work and ask than it is to try to go back and fix a mistake. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Read the rules before posting there. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- They are strict on certain things to preserve the legality of their website. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- It is not a whole lot like smoked DMT. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- But it will give you a little idea of what you are in for. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Well fill out this questionnaire and post it at DMT World. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Someone will usually be able to help you troubleshoot it. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- There is a possibility that you can still recover your material. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- I highly recommend that you read all of the teks available on the Internet not just this one. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Read and re read them get to know the process well. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Don t use it unless you have absolutely no other choice. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Do a small amount first to get the hang of the process. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Blowing 1 8 of a pound of material is not nearly as depressing as blowing all of it. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- You will most likely make a few mistakes on your first extraction anyway. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Have a hand on it to steady the thing. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Make absolutely sure your valve on your separatory funnel is closed before you pour liquid in. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Seems simple but you ll be surprised how often people forget to check this. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Do it a little at a time. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- I go through about 15 filters from start to end on a extraction like the one in the guide. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- It s almost like typing paper. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Thus the pores clog up rather quickly. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Evaporation is a pain in the ass. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- Try your best to find a area that has decent ventilation but no dust. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- I know that s a tall order but your material is very exposed and tiny gnats and dust particles seem to be attracted to it like a magnet. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- I know there are many teks out there that vary widely in how they do their extraction. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- You have to keep in mind that many of these teks are over 5 years old. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- There has been a lot of new advancements and refinements in DMT extraction over the last few years. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- I am not saying the teks are no good, they are still quite effective, but they may not be up to date on recent discoveries. _Vovin's_tek.html_
- It seems like one would lose some DMT from the material with all the filtering, recrystallizations and washes. _Vovin's_tek.html_

- Chemical and physical properties Effects When salvinorin A is absorbed through the oral mucosa the first effects are usually experienced in 5-10 min. _Salvinorin.html_
- The strength of the effects builds very quickly over a few minutes, maintaining a plateau for about 1 h. _Salvinorin.html_
- The effects gradually subside over another l-h period. _Salvinorin.html_
- The evolution of effects over time is identical to that of orally ingested S. divinorum leaves. _Salvinorin.html_
- There is almost no transition period experienced. _Salvinorin.html_
- The strongest effects last 5-10 min and then gradually subside over about 20-30 min. _Salvinorin.html_
- A similar evolution of effects is reported for smoked S. divinorum leaves. _Salvinorin.html_
- Although variable in duration, the effects experienced have the same overall characteristics regardless of the route of absorption used. _Salvinorin.html_
- The nature of the effects experienced depends on many factors including dose, set and setting. _Salvinorin.html_
- Frequently people report having seen visions of people, objects, and places. _Salvinorin.html_
- Occasionally individuals get up and move about with no apparent awareness of their movements or behavior. _Salvinorin.html_
- Some individuals speak gibberish during the most intense phase of the experience, others laugh hysterically. _Salvinorin.html_
- Certain themes are common to many of the visions and sensations described. _Salvinorin.html_
- The following is a listing of some of the more common themes: Becoming objects (yellow plaid French fries, fresh paint, a drawer, a pant leg, a Ferris wheel, etc.). _Salvinorin.html_
- Visions of various two dimensional surfaces, films and membranes. _Salvinorin.html_
- Revisiting places from the past, especially childhood. _Salvinorin.html_
- Loss of the body and or identity. _Salvinorin.html_
- Various sensations of motion, or being pulled or twisted by forces of some kind. _Salvinorin.html_
- Uncontrollable hysterical laughter. _Salvinorin.html_
- Overlapping realities. _Salvinorin.html_
- The perception that one is in several locations at once. _Salvinorin.html_
- Some of the effects appear to parallel those of other hallucinogens (i.e. the depersonalization experienced with ketamine, the rapid onset of effects and short duration of smoked DMT). _Salvinorin.html_
- The volunteers who were experienced with other hallucinogens all agreed that despite some similarities, the content of the visions and the overall character of the experience is quite unique. _Salvinorin.html_

- The Core of the Heating Element The Shell of the Heating Element Constructing the Heating Element For the core: Place ceramic fiber onto a screen. _The_Inspirator_mkII.html_

- Fold the screen to clasp the fiber. _The_Inspirator_mkII.html_
- Begin to roll the screen by folding an end. _The_Inspirator_mkII.html_
- Roll the screen tightly. _The_Inspirator_mkII.html_
- For the shell: Firmly hold the tip of a chopstick in the middle of the screen. _The_Inspirator_mkII.html_
- Bend the sides up around the tip. _The_Inspirator_mkII.html_
- Bend the ends ups while holding the sides in place to cradle the tip of the chopstick. _The_Inspirator_mkII.html_
- Place the core in the shell to create the element. _The_Inspirator_mkII.html_

- The element could also be rolled around between fingertips to help reduce the springiness it may have when attempting to insert into the end of the bowl or dropper stem. _The_Inspirator_mkII.html_
- Variations in Design As ceramic fiber may not be readily available, it may be omitted and replaced with a second screen rolled up for the core for the Night Elf variation in technique and design, vice the Spiceliner variation which utilizes ceramic fiber. _The_Inspirator_mkII.html_

- The root of this plant has been and is still to this day consumed by many pacific islanders from New Guinea all the way to Hawaii and down into french Polynesia. _Kava.html_
- Its primary use is as a sedative and a anxiolytic with many other tradional medicinal remedies. _Kava.html_
- The primary active ingredients are in the root and are a series of kavalactones witch is concentrated in the roots but found also in lower amounts in the leaves and stems. _Kava.html_

- Contents 1Morphology 2Cultivation 3Preparation and consumption 3.1Traditional 3.2Western Preparation 3.3Pills and extracts 4Chemistry and active principles 4.1Lactones 4.2Flavokavains and other compounds 4.3Chemotypes 5Pharmacodynamics 6Effects 6.1side effects 6.2Liver Toxicity 7Kava in traditional pharmacopoeia and medicine 7.1Traditional medicinal uses by region 8Ethnobotanical heritage Morphology Piper Methysticum is a member of the pepper family, Piperaceae, which belongs to the order Piperales in the class Dicotyledonae. _Kava.html_
- Ten of these in the Piperaceae species are products of human consumption used as spices or medicinal drugs. these include: P. nigrum (Pepper), one of the oldest known spices, P. betle P. cubeba (java pepper or tailed pepper), a plant native to indonesia wich was formerly used as a medicine and now as a spice. _Kava.html_
- It is a hardy, slow growing Perennial reaching heights of more then 3 meters. _Kava.html_
- It is harvested for its rootstock or stump with Monopedial stems with sympodial branches growing from the stump. _Kava.html_
- The stump is knotty, Think, and sometimes tuberous. _Kava.html_
- From this rootstock extends laterally up to 3 meteres long. _Kava.html_
- Rootstock color varies between white to dark yellowdepending upon the amount of kavalactones that are contained in the lemon yellow resin. _Kava.html_
- Cultivation Although kava does produce flowers it is incapable of reproducing sexually; its propagation is vegetatively and is dependent solely on human effort. _Kava.html_
- Farmers take cuttings from existing stems off harvested plants and planted i the ground somewhat sideways. _Kava.html_
- New growth occurs at the stem bud at the axil of a lateral branch scar. _Kava.html_
- An upright shoot develops, and then axillary buds and lateral axes appear. _Kava.html_
- In the same way the root stock develops. _Kava.html_
- Choose a site away from prevailing winds air currents can damage kava stems and rootstock, making them susceptible to disease. _Kava.html_
- Along with adequate shade and protection from the wind, kava requires fairly high average temperatures (20-35c) and high humidity (70-100 ). _Kava.html_
- Kave grows best in deep, friable, well-draining soils that are rich in organic matter. _Kava.html_
- The plant is very nutrient demanding. _Kava.html_
- Preparation and consumption Traditional In the Pacific kava is typically drunk at dusk, usually before the evening meal.Infused kava is never kept for long; Islanders prepare kava for immediate consumption. _Kava.html_
- After drinking, people eat small amounts of food because kava tends to reduce appetite and over eating can cause nausea. _Kava.html_
- Several traditional methods of kava preparation all serve to extract the active chemical constitutes of fresh or dried rootstock. _Kava.html_
- Processing  involves chewing, grating, grinding or pounding kava stumps and roots and then infusing the processes mass into cold water. _Kava.html_
- These methods break up and macerate the rootstock so that the kavalactones after more readily released in the cold water. _Kava.html_
- Today mastication of fresh rootstock is only practiced in southern vanauatu and among some tribes in papua new guinea. _Kava.html_
- In Fiji men serving as village priests prepared kava every morning in men s houseshouses, or houses of ancestor worship, as an offering tho village ancestors. _Kava.html_
- The priests and other men in the village would then drink kava together. _Kava.html_
- The rootstock was prepared by grinding, not mastication, and the drink was infused in lead lines holes in the ground, in shallow wooden bowls that were sometimes human or animal in shape, of in plain clay vessels. _Kava.html_
- Early fijians folders their kava by pouring it through bunches of backen fern leaves in a wooden canister like device, rather then using a stronger of hibiscus tiliaceus bark as is common in Polynesia. _Kava.html_
- Fijians also did not drink our of coconut shells as they do today, but instead right out of the container. _Kava.html_
- In traditional samoan preperation, a young girl chased and served kava. _Kava.html_
- The girl was preferably a virgin, who purified herself for kava preparation by washing her hands and wrists. _Kava.html_
- After chewing kava, she mixed and infused the macerated root in a kava bowl and filtered out the residue with a hibiscus bark strainer. _Kava.html_
- Samoan ceremony required the girl to sit cross legged and bare breasted on a mat behind the kava bowl, with flowers carefully arranged in her hair and wearing a grass skirt. _Kava.html_
- This presented an image of beauty that added to the aesthetic dimension of kava preparation. _Kava.html_
- It the banks island of northern Vanuatu, Kava drinkers traditionally split into 2 groups, And a person from each group prepare kava for the other. _Kava.html_
- As on most of the northern Vanuatu islands, preparation in the banks group involved the grinding of fresh kava over a large wooden dish using an elongated coral abrading stone. _Kava.html_
- The inner surfaces of these wooden dishes eventually became covered with a grayish-green deposit that is also found at the bottom of coconut shells used as drinking bowls. _Kava.html_
- This deposit is a resinous kavalactone residue that contains the plants active ingredients in concentrated form. _Kava.html_
- Western Preparation Kava preparation in the western world outside of the islands is a climbing trend with the emergence of natural products becoming more and more popular. _Kava.html_
- Kava has moved from a ceremonial sense to more of a medicine with ease of use, from extracts of all solvents to pharmaceutical tablets with kavalactones as there main ingredient. _Kava.html_
- In Western countries, kava is usually made from kava root powder or extracts. _Kava.html_
- Generally, 2 tablespoons of powder is added per 8 oz. of water, but multiple tablespoons per 16 oz. of water to increase potency. _Kava.html_
- The powder is then put into a muslin bag or nylon sock and soaked in water for about 30 minutes to allow the water to completely soak through the powdered fibers, after a thorough soaking the rootstock is then massaged for a few minutes under the water for a few minutes with breaks to squeeze the powder dry and repeating till the water is a creamy brown color.Lecithin is often added to aid in the process of emulsifying the kavalactones with water. _Kava.html_
- Another popular method is blending. _Kava.html_
- Blended in a blender for several minutes then strained into a straining cloth; Nylon, cheesecloth, and silk screen are common materials for straining. _Kava.html_
- The remaining liquid is squeezed from the pulp and then the process is repeated until one last strain and squeeze of the pulp and the rest is discarded. _Kava.html_

- Chemistry and active principles Kavalactones are the main principle chemicals that give the desired effects from kava. _Kava.html_
- Lactones These chemicals are mostly, if not entirely, contained in its resin. _Kava.html_
- These molecules are a series of lactones-that is, organic compounds containing oxygen, with similar structures. _Kava.html_
- These are alpha- pyrones bearing a methoxyl group at carbon 4 and an aromatic styryl moiety at carbon 6. _Kava.html_
- Butyrolactone, an example of a lactone ring. _Kava.html_
- The skeletons of the lactonic molecules isolated from kava rootstock are generally 4- methoxy-2- pyrones with phenyl or styryl substitutions at the 6- position. _Kava.html_
- They consider of 13 carbon atoms, 6 of which from a benzene ring attached by a double bond to an unsaturated lactone. _Kava.html_
- 15 lactones have been isolated from kava rootstock, 9 of which have been fully identified. _Kava.html_
- The following 6 compounds are present in the highest concentrations: yangonin, methysticin, dihydromethystic, kavain, dihydrokavain, and demethoxy-yangonin. _Kava.html_
- 9 other compounds are of minor importance in the rootstock: dehydrokavain, cis-5-hydroxy-kavain, 7,8-dihydroyangonin, 5,6-dihydroyangonin, 5,6-dehydro-methysticin, 11-methoxy-yangonin, 11-hydroxy-yangonin, 11-methoxy-12-hydroxy-dehydro-kavain, and 10-methoxy-yangonin. _Kava.html_
- Some researchers have tried to classify kavalactones by reference to common characteristics. _Kava.html_
- The simplest method of grouping is one suggested by hänsel, which supports the molecules according to the presence or absence of double bonds at the 5,6 and 7,8 positions and divided them into 2 major groups: the enolides, with 1 double bond, and the dienolides, with 2 double bonds. _Kava.html_
- This system recognizes that primary chemical differences among the kavalactones involve the presence or absence of these double bonds as well as the presence or absence of substituent groups in the phenyl ring. _Kava.html_
- Kavain, one of the active kavalactones present in Kava Kava root Flavokavains and other compounds 3 flavokavains labeled A, B , and C, have been identified in kava rootstock. _Kava.html_
- Flavokavain C structure and synthesis were analyzed by a Indian team in 1976. _Kava.html_
- Other substances isolated from the kava plant include an alcohol, ketones, a phytosterol, and organic acids. _Kava.html_
- Chemotypes In 1984 Lebot and Lévesque initiated a research program to address 2 questions about the chemistry of kava. _Kava.html_
- Lebot and Lévesque s identification of a number of kava chemotype groups also provides additional insights into the pre history of distribution of the plant. _Kava.html_
- Their findings showed that chemotypes are genetically controlled and therefore constitute a genetic fingerprint for each cultivar, and that species domestication involved preservation of selected chemotypes by cloning. _Kava.html_
- Lebot and Lévesque divided the active principles into 2 main groups-major and minor kavalactones-and demonstrated that the former for approximately 96 of the lipid extract. _Kava.html_
- They therefore numbered and only used the major kavalactones (1 demethoxy-yangonin, DMY; 2 dihydrokavain, DHK; 3 yangonin, y; 4 kavain, k; 5 dihydromethystic, DHM; and 6 methysticin M) to define cultivar chemotypes. _Kava.html_
- These 6 active substances comprise a natural cocktail that induces different physiological effects according to the particular kavalactone mixture. _Kava.html_
- To identify the different mixtures offered by various cultivars, chemical compositions were coded by listing in decreasing order of proportion the 6 major kavalactones in the extract; this coded description is called a chemotype. _Kava.html_
- For example, if the chemotype of a cultivar is 521364, this indicates that kavalactone number 5 (DHM) has the highest content of the 6 lactones in that cultivar, kavalactone number 2 (DHK) has the second highest content, and so on. _Kava.html_
- Chemotype 521634 produced distinct physiological effects that differ from those of the other chemotypes. _Kava.html_
- The first 3 kavalactones in the code usually represent 70 of the total. _Kava.html_
- These 3, therefore, are typically the most important for characterizing the chemotype. _Kava.html_
- In some cultivars, the percentage of each of the 3 major kavalactones is about the same. _Kava.html_
- Pharmacodynamics Effects of kavalactones include mild sedation, a slight numbing of the gums and mouth, and vivid dreams. _Kava.html_
- Kava has been reported to improve cognitive performance and promote a cheerful mood. _Kava.html_
- Kava has similar effects to benzodiazepine medications, including muscle relaxant, anaesthetic, anticonvulsive and anxiolytic effects. _Kava.html_
- They are thought to result from direct interactions of kavalactones with voltage-gated ion channels. _Kava.html_
- It is thought to do this via modulating GABA activity via altering the lipid membrane structure and sodium channel function. _Kava.html_
- However, it has also been shown that administration of the GABA antagonist Flumazenil does not have an antagonistic effect on kavalactones, suggesting that an alternative pathway may be involved. _Kava.html_
- Heavy, long-term kava use does not cause any reduction of ability in saccade and cognitive tests, but is associated with elevated liver enzymes. _Kava.html_

- Name The name of this organisation shall be: Earthship Nexus Inc. _Constitution.html_
- Definitions Throughout this Constitution, unless the context otherwise indicates, the following terms shall have the meanings set against them: the Association Earthship Nexus Inc. fiscal year A period commencing on the date of incorporation of the Association and ending on 31 December; and thereafter each period commencing 1 January and ending 31 December in the same year. _Constitution.html_
- General Meeting Annual General Meeting or other Ordinary or Special General Meeting. special resolution A resolution is a special resolution if it is passed by a majority of not less than three-quarters of the members of the Association who are entitled under the rules of the Association to vote and vote in person. _Constitution.html_
- Encampment A plot of land owned, leased, or otherwise occupied, or intended to be occupied, by the Association for use by its members. _Constitution.html_
- Objects The objects of the Association shall be as follows: To be an organised association of individuals interested in sustainable living, permaculture and organic farming. _Constitution.html_
- To establish one or more Encampments in which to advance these interests. _Constitution.html_
- To cooperate with all bodies of similar aims. _Constitution.html_
- The property and income of the Association shall be applied solely towards the advancement of the objects of the Association and no part of that property or income may be paid or otherwise distributed, directly or indirectly, to any person or body, except in good faith in the advancements of those objects. _Constitution.html_
- Executive The Executive of the Association shall consist of the following members: The President The Vice-President The Secretary The Treasurer 5. _Constitution.html_
- Committee The Association shall be governed by the Committee. _Constitution.html_
- The committee of the Association shall consist of the following members: The President The Vice-President The Secretary The Treasurer Three Ordinary Committee Members 6. _Constitution.html_
- Membership Membership is open to any person who shares the aims of the Association and agrees to comply with the Constitution and rules of the Association. _Constitution.html_
- A subscription fee for ordinary membership may be payable to the Association if decided upon by the Committee. _Constitution.html_
- Honorary Life Membership The Association in General Meeting may be a two-third majority of those present and voting confer Honorary Life Membership upon any member who has performed outstanding service to the Association. _Constitution.html_
- Election The following members of the Committee shall be elected at the Annual General Meeting: The President The Vice-President The Secretary The Treasurer Three Ordinary Committee Members The secretary shall call for nominations for the above positions at least ten days before the date of the Annual General Meeting. _Constitution.html_
- The nominations shall close at that meeting. _Constitution.html_
- Only members who have held a previously held a position on the Committee may be nominated for an Executive position, unless no such members are nominated. _Constitution.html_
- Duration of Office The members of the Committee shall remain in office until the close of the succeeding Annual General Meeting, except as elsewhere provided in the Constitution. _Constitution.html_
- Exercise of Powers The Committee shall only exercise its powers at a properly convened meeting of the Committee, except as elsewhere provided in the Constitution. _Constitution.html_
- Powers of the Association The Association may do all things necessary of convenient for carrying out its objects and purposes, and in particular, may: acquire, hold, deal with, and dispose of any real or personal property; open and operate bank accounts; invest its money: in any security in which trust monies may lawfully be invested; or in any manner authorised by the rules of the Association; borrow money or incur overdrafts provided always that the total long term liabilities of the Association shall not exceed one fifth of the Association s money holdings, unless otherwise approved by a General Meeting; give such security for the discharge for the discharge of liabilities by the Association as the Association sees fit; appoint agents to transact any business of the Association on its behalf; enter into any other contract it considers necessary or desirable; and act as trustee and accept and hold real and personal property upon trust, but does not have the power to do any act or thing as a trustee that, if done otherwise than as a trustee, would contravene the rules of the Association. _Constitution.html_
- Proceedings of Committee 1. _Constitution.html_
- Ordinary Meetings The Committee shall meet physically or electronically at least once a month at such times and places as the President or the Committee may determine. _Constitution.html_
- All members are entitled to attend these meetings unless otherwise specified in this Constitution. _Constitution.html_
- Notice of Meetings The Secretary shall cause all members of the Committee to receive written or email notice of any meeting of the Committee at least four days before the date of the meeting. _Constitution.html_
- Special Meetings The Secretary shall forthwith call a meeting of the Committee upon receiving a written requisition from at least three members thereof; and such special meetings shall be held not later than seven days immediately following the receipt of such requisition. _Constitution.html_
- Quorum The quorum for a meeting of the Committee shall be four members of the Committee at least two of whom are members of the Executive. _Constitution.html_
- Clause 14.5.1 does not apply with respect to a pecuniary interest that exists only by virtue of the fact that the member of the Committee is an employee of the Association. _Constitution.html_
- Voting Only members of the Committee are entitled to vote at a meeting of the Committee, unless otherwise decided by the Committee on a per-motion basis. _Constitution.html_
- Private Meetings The Committee may decide by majority vote to exclude non-Committee members from part of a meeting if not doing so would be likely to unfairly disclose confidential information regarding any member of the Association to any other member. _Constitution.html_
- Duties of Committee Members 1. _Constitution.html_
- President In addition to any other provisions set out elsewhere in this Constitution, or any regulation or policy made thereunder, it shall be the duty of the President: to conduct the relations of the Association with other organisations and to the general public subject to the authority of the Committee; to coordinate and supervise the work of the Vice-President, Secretary, Treasurer, and other officers of the Association subject to the authority of the Committee. _Constitution.html_
- Vice-President In addition to any other provisions set out elsewhere in this Constitution, or any regulation or policy made thereunder, it shall be the duty of the Vice President: to assist in the President s duties; to carry out Presidential duties during the absence of the President, during which time the Vice-President shall be deemed to be the President. _Constitution.html_
- Treasurer In addition to any other provisions set out elsewhere in this Constitution, or any regulation or policy made thereunder, it shall be the duty of the Treasurer: to be responsible for the receipt of all moneys paid to or received by, or by him or her on behalf of, the Association and issue receipts for those moneys in the name of the Association; to keep accounting records that correctly record and explain the financial transactions and financial position of the Association, in such a manner that permits convenient and proper auditing; to render an account at each meeting of the Committee of all receipts and payments since the previous meeting; to render an account of the petty cash at each meeting of the committee; to furnish the Committee with such other accounts and information relating to the finances of the Association as the Committee may require; to present a current financial statement showing all receipts and payments at each Ordinary General Meeting and by motion of Committee, an auditor s report at the Annual General Meeting; and unless the members resolve otherwise at a general meeting, have custody of all securities, books and documents of a financial nature and accounting records of the Association. _Constitution.html_
- Ordinary Committee Members Ordinary Committee Members will have no additional duties than those set out elsewhere in this Constitution. _Constitution.html_
- Resignation Any officer of the Association may resign from a position by giving written notification to the Secretary at least fourteen days before that Officer s resignation takes effect. _Constitution.html_
- Absence The Committee shall declare vacant the position of any member of the Committee if that member has been absent from two consecutive meetings of the Committee withotu giving a satisfactory explanation for that absence. _Constitution.html_
- Election If any position on the Committee becomes vacant then the Committee shall call a General Meeting for the election of a member to that position within four weeks of that position becoming vacant. _Constitution.html_
- Ordinary General Meeting There shall be at least one General Meeting in each year, namely the Annual General Meeting, and any Ordinary General Meetings held as the Committee shall determine. _Constitution.html_
- Notice of Meeting The secretary shall make all reasonable attempts to notify all members using at least a notice on the Association web site for ten days preceding the meeting and an email sent to all addresses on the membership register at least ten days before the date of the meeting. _Constitution.html_
- Special General Meeting The Committee may at any time, without the need for a Committee meeting, call a Special General Meeting of the Association by the written agreement of at least 3 Committee members, at least one of whom is a member of the Executive. _Constitution.html_
- General Meeting Called by Ordinary Members The Secretary shall forthwith call a Special General Meeting upon receiving a written requisition from at least ten ordinary members of the Association and such meetings shall be held with appropriate notice requirement and not later than 17 days immediately following the receipt of such requisition. _Constitution.html_
- Powers of a General Meeting A general meeting may exercise the same powers as the Committee except for those powers exclusively reserved for the Committee under this Constitution. _Constitution.html_
- Agenda The Secretary shall post the agenda for any General Meeting on the web site alongside the notice of meeting at least four days before the date of the meeting. _Constitution.html_
- Quorum The quorum of a General Meeting shall be fifteen ordinary members present in person or electronically. _Constitution.html_
- Chair The President shall have the right to take the Chair at any General meeting or meetings of the Committee. _Constitution.html_
- If the President is absent or does not wish to exercise this right at any meeting, that right shall be held by the Vice-President; if refused, that meeting shall elect its own Chair. _Constitution.html_
- Voting Except where stated otherwise in this Constitution, all members of the Association are entitled to vote a General Meeting. _Constitution.html_
- Members may attend and vote electronically if electronic presence can reasonably be provided. _Constitution.html_
- Postal voting or proxy voting is not permitted. _Constitution.html_
- Procedure for Motions Once a motion is tabled, the motion shall be open to general discussion and ammendments. _Constitution.html_
- After general discussion, a call for votes will be made by the Chair of the meeting. _Constitution.html_
- Any member at the meeting may call for the votes to be by secret ballot. _Constitution.html_
- Removal From Office The Committee may request any member of the Committee, member of any sub-committee, officer, representative or delegate of the Assocation to resign from that position if a person has failed to perform satisfactorily the normal duties of the position. _Constitution.html_
- The person concerned shall be informed of this request at least seven days before a meeting of the Committee where that person may speak on their own behalf. _Constitution.html_
- Any such request shall require such a motion which will only be passed if a two-thirds majority of those voting have voted in favor of the motion. _Constitution.html_
- The request to resign shall be delivered in writing to the person concern forthwith. _Constitution.html_
- If a person who has not resigned within seven days of the request the Committee may declare that position vacant. _Constitution.html_
- Any person who has had their former position declared vacant shall have the right to appeal to a General Meeting for their reinstatement. _Constitution.html_
- A two-thirds majority of a committee meeting may cancel a membership by passing a motion to that effect. _Constitution.html_
- The cancellation of membership shall be delivered in writing to the person concerned forthwith. _Constitution.html_
- Any person who has their membership cancelled shall have the right to appeal to a General Meeting for the reinstatement of their membership, except where that person is a first-time member of the Association and has been a member for less than one month or has had their membership cancelled by Committee more than once. _Constitution.html_
- A person who has had their membership cancelled may not reapply for membership for the period of one year. _Constitution.html_
- Finance All money due and payable to the Association shall be received by the Treasurer who shall lodge it without undue delay in the account of the Association. _Constitution.html_
- Except as otherwise provided for in the Constitution, or in a policy, any two of the Executive shall be empowered jointly to sign cheques and forms of authority for the withdrawal of any money standing in the credit of the Association in the account of the Association. _Constitution.html_
- The Committee may by a two-thirds majority elect a single delegate from the Committee who may sign in lieu of one of the required Executive signatures on a cheque. _Constitution.html_
- No payment shall be made on behalf of or in the name of the Association unless it has been authorised by the Committee. _Constitution.html_
- The Committee may, outside a Committee meeting, agree to a payment or purchase by written consent of five Committee members including at least two Executive members of the Committee. _Constitution.html_
- Policy The Association in General Meeting may make policy on any matter relating to the conduct of the affairs of the Association provided that policy is not inconsistent with or repugnant to this Constitution or the Act. _Constitution.html_
- Any motion proposing to make, alter or rescind policy shall require written notice and shall only be passed by special resolution at a General Meeting. _Constitution.html_
- The policy of the Association shall form an appendix to this Constitution and be made available with it. _Constitution.html_
- Interpretation The Committee shall be the sole authority for interpreting the meaning of any of the provisions contained in this Constitution or in any regulation of the Association policy made thereunder. _Constitution.html_
- Ammendments to the Constitution The Association in a General Meeting may amend this Constitution. _Constitution.html_
- Any motion proposing to amend this Constitution shall require a written notice of motion and any such motion shall only be passed by special resolution. _Constitution.html_
- An alteration of the Constitution of the Association does not take effect until sub-rule 25.3 is complied with. _Constitution.html_
- Interim Measures The Executive shall have the power to suspend such provisions of this Constitution until the 1st January, 2013 as may be expedient to the formation of an Association. _Constitution.html_
- Commercial Exploitation No member of the Association shall use any of the resources of the Association for direct financial gain. _Constitution.html_
- Inspection of Documents and Records The Secretary shall make available to any member of the public a copy of this Constitution for perusal. _Constitution.html_
- A member may at any reasonable time inspect without charge the books, documents, records and securities of the Association. _Constitution.html_
- Make sure to monitor our mailing list for any updates Erroneous requests: When erroneous requests are sent to the API, a HTTP header will be sent with the key MediaWiki-API-Error and then both the value of the header and the error code sent back will be set to the same value In the case of an invalid action being passed, these will have a value of unknown_action For more information see Documentation: FAQ Mailing list: Api Announcements: Bugs Requests: Parameters: format - The format of the output One value: json, jsonfm, php, phpfm, wddx, wddxfm, xml, xmlfm, yaml, yamlfm, rawfm, txt, txtfm, dbg, dbgfm, dump, dumpfm, none Default: xmlfm action - What action you would like to perform. _api_php.html_

- To save actions causing any more site replication lag, this parameter can make the client wait until the replication lag is less than the specified value. _api_php.html_
- In case of a replag error, error code maxlag is returned, with the message like Waiting for host: lag seconds lagged n . _api_php.html_
- See for more information smaxage - Set the s-maxage header to this many seconds. _api_php.html_
- Errors are never cached Default: 0 maxage - Set the max-age header to this many seconds. _api_php.html_
- Errors are never cached Default: 0 requestid - Request ID to distinguish requests. _api_php.html_

- This is to prevent password guessing by automated password crackers This module only accepts POST requests Parameters: lgname - User Name lgpassword - Password lgdomain - Domain (optional) lgtoken - Login token obtained in first request Example: api.php?action login lgname user lgpassword password action logout Log out and clear session data Example: Log the current user out: api.php?action logout action createaccount Create a new user account. _api_php.html_
- This module requires write rights This module only accepts POST requests Parameters: name - Username This parameter is required password - Password (ignored if mailpassword is set) domain - Domain for external authentication (optional) token - Account creation token obtained in first request email - Email address of user (optional) realname - Real name of user (optional) mailpassword - If set to any value, a random password will be emailed to the user reason - Optional reason for creating the account to be put in the logs language - Language code to set as default for the user (optional, defaults to content language) Examples: api.php?action createaccount name testuser password test123api.php?action createaccount name testmailuser mailpassword true reason MyReason action query Query API module allows applications to get needed pieces of data from the MediaWiki databases, and is loosely based on the old query.php interface. _api_php.html_
- All data modifications will first have to use query to acquire a token to prevent abuse from malicious sites This module requires read rights Parameters: prop - Which properties to get for the titles revisions pageids. _api_php.html_
- Module help is available below Values (separate with ): categories, categoryinfo, duplicatefiles, extlinks, images, imageinfo, info, links, iwlinks, langlinks, pageprops, revisions, stashimageinfo, templates list - Which lists to get. _api_php.html_
- Module help is available below Values (separate with ): allcategories, allfileusages, allimages, alllinks, allpages, alltransclusions, allusers, backlinks, blocks, categorymembers, deletedrevs, embeddedin, exturlusage, filearchive, imageusage, iwbacklinks, langbacklinks, logevents, pageswithprop, pagepropnames, protectedtitles, querypage, random, recentchanges, , tags, usercontribs, users, watchlist, watchlistraw meta - Which metadata to get about the site. _api_php.html_
- Module help is available below Values (separate with ): allmessages, siteinfo, userinfo, filerepoinfo indexpageids - Include an additional pageids section listing all returned page IDs export - Export the current revisions of all given or generated pages exportnowrap - Return the export XML without wrapping it in an XML result (same format as Special:Export). _api_php.html_
- This parameter is recommended for all new development, and will be made default in the next API version. titles - A list of titles to work on Separate values with Maximum number of values 50 (500 for bots) pageids - A list of page IDs to work on Separate values with Maximum number of values 50 (500 for bots) revids - A list of revision IDs to work on Separate values with Maximum number of values 50 (500 for bots) redirects - Automatically resolve redirects converttitles - Convert titles to other variants if necessary. _api_php.html_

- Languages that support variant conversion include gan, iu, kk, ku, shi, sr, tg, uz, zh generator - Get the list of pages to work on by executing the specified query module. _api_php.html_
- Useful for checking whether a certain page is in a certain category Separate values with Maximum number of values 50 (500 for bots) cldir - The direction in which to list One value: ascending, descending Default: ascending Examples: Get a list of categories Albert Einstein belongs to: api.php?action query prop categories titles Albert 20Einstein Get information about all categories used in the Albert Einstein : api.php?action query generator categories titles Albert 20Einstein prop info Generator: This module may be used as a generator prop categoryinfo (ci) Returns information about the given categories This module requires read rights Parameters: cicontinue - When more results are available, use this to continue Example: api.php?action query prop categoryinfo titles Category:Foo Category:Bar prop duplicatefiles (df) List all files that are duplicates of the given file(s) based on hash values This module requires read rights Parameters: dflimit - How many duplicate files to return No more than 500 (5000 for bots) allowed Default: 10 dfcontinue - When more results are available, use this to continue dfdir - The direction in which to list One value: ascending, descending Default: ascending dflocalonly - Look only for files in the local repository Examples: api.php?action query titles File:Albert_Einstein_Head.jpg prop duplicatefilesapi.php?action query generator allimages prop duplicatefiles Generator: This module may be used as a generator prop extlinks (el) Returns all external URLs (not interwikis) from the given page(s) This module requires read rights Parameters: ellimit - How many links to return No more than 500 (5000 for bots) allowed Default: 10 eloffset - When more results are available, use this to continue elprotocol - Protocol of the URL. _api_php.html_
- If empty and elquery set, the protocol is http. _api_php.html_
- Leave both this and elquery empty to list all external links Can be empty, or One value: http, https, ftp, ftps, ssh, sftp, irc, ircs, xmpp, sip, sips, gopher, telnet, nntp, worldwind, mailto, tel, sms, news, svn, git, mms, bitcoin, magnet, urn, geo Default: elquery -  string without protocol. _api_php.html_

- Therefore the absorption maximum is shifted to the right and has a bigger width. _Text_Meskalin_txt.html_
- Now attaching a Methoxy group (5-MeO-...) or Hydroxy group (Bufo) will further increase the peak width. _Text_Meskalin_txt.html_
- When finally moving to Harmalas the pi system has the biggest size, therefore the absorption is so far extended that we start seeing this compound as being colourfull. _Text_Meskalin_txt.html_

- Acacia greggii From DMT-Nexus Wiki Jump to: navigation,  Contents 1General Plant Info 2Geographic Distribution 3Identification 4Alkaloid content 5Extraction 6Other uses 7Cultivation 8Suppliers 9Links 10Reference General Plant Info A low shrub which flowers from April to June Common names include Catclaw Acacia, Catclaw Mesquite, Gregg s Catclaw, Devil s Claw, Paradise Flower, Wait-a-minute Tree, and Wait-a-bit Tree; these names mostly come from the fact that the tree has numerous hooked prickles with the shape and size of a cat s claw, that tend to hook onto passers-by; the hooked person must stop ( wait a minute ) to remove the prickles carefully to avoid injury or shredded clothing. (Note: Cat s Claw is also used to refer to Uncaria tomentosa, a woody vine found in the tropical jungles of South and Central America). _Acacia_greggii.html_

- Other ergolines From DMT-Nexus Wiki Jump to: navigation,  Other ergolines the ergot molecuul is pretty fragile and decomposes easy in some moist light (some)air , the 3 best spots to change improve the coumpound stabilitiet is reanforce at the most stable parts...those are the Nitrogens..in the moleculair ergot structur you see 3 N s , these are the nitrogens, one is at the bottom (position 1) , nr 2 is in the mid right position called position nr 6 and the third one is near the top connected to position 8 ( the positions are the number you get when you start counting the connections on the outside of the molecule anti-clockwise , try it !. people have tried to add more atoms elements to the N s possitions and one such experiment was hoffman 25th try for a new compound eventually known as lsd....but here are some lesser know other samples : 1)on the 8 position : - some of the lysergic precursors : methysergide, ergometrine and metyl-ergmetrine are slightly active above 1-4 mg. it still unknown if these can cause gangreen nercosis in certain people. source (J.ott in Pharmacotheon ) -(S)Lasba : a stereoselective butyl analoog on the 8-amide has been found active in humans a few years ago, but mostly act as a stimulant (source : perdue-uni nichols personal exprience) nice info to be found here : url -also the morpholine and methyl-ethyl-amide moity are active (hoffman stoll at sandoz, and shulgin mentions it in Tihkal.) on the 6 position : AL-LAD, BU-LAD, CYP-LAD, ETH-LAD, PRO-LAD and a few others, Mostly developed by Nichols but in coalition with Shulgin. promising : - future research is being done to replace the carboxylic acid to a thoiacid this means at the top the oxygen will be repaced with a sulphur( thio) and then there is still room for the N-diethyl amide. _Other_ergolines.html_

- 6-apdb From DMT-Nexus Wiki Jump to: navigation,  Safety profile Category: Psychedelic Stimulant Main effects: Open and closed eye visuals including color enhancement and light fractal like visuals similar to DMT but not all as overwhelming or all encompassing (probably increases with dosage in terms of depth of visual experience), euphoria, change in perception of time, heightened senses (smell, audio, and touch) Side effects: Nausea, increased sweating dehydration, dilation of pupils(very noticeable), unusual body sensations (facial flushing, chills, goosebumps, body energy), increased blood pressure and heart rate is reported by the few reports found online - although noted at one point during come up a drop in heart rate, difficulty focusing at times, jaw clenching, may decrease motor skills in terms of ability to steady hands IE: slight tremors (probably increasing with dosage), paranoia, fear, and panic, dystonia (rare), seizure (rare), death (rare) Health risks: 6-apdb is a very new substance, with little known about its pharmacological or behavioral risks. _6-apdb.html_ [x2]
